messages:
incident-bot: [SEV-2] Elevated 5xx and latency for model variant `rwd-llama-lite-v2f` in eu-west-1. Error rate +18% over baseline, tail latency >1.2s. Auto-slo-fallback triggered. Pager -> @sara oncall.

sara: acked. jumping in. seeing spikes in /v1/chat/gen for a subset of customer keys. any recent deploys to that variant?

mike: nothing deploy-wise from eng-runtime in the last 6hrs. we rolled a quantized kernel yesterday but that was for `v3beta` not v2f.

sara: load looks concentrated on a handful of heavy keys. hitting the same predictor pods, cache misses are high.

ops-bot: active mitigations available: `disable-variant`, `route-redistribute`, `apply-key-quota`, `soft-throttle`. Suggested next step: reduce weight of v2f to 0 and move traffic to `stable-llama-v2`.

sara: ok plan: 1) temporarily disable v2f for public traffic 2) redirect canary/experimental keys to stable 3) apply per-key emergency quota for the heavy keys 4) handoff after stabilization. doing step 1 now.

mike: +1. make sure we keep an emergency backstop variant with quantized fallback enabled.

sara: running command in control plane:
```
redwoodctl rollout set-weight --model rwd-llama-lite --variant v2f --weight 0 --reason "emergency: high 5xx"
```

ops-bot: rollout accepted. weight change in progress. expected drain ~ 30s.

jess: on standby for handoff. any visible customer-impact so I can call out to CS?

sara: early check: ~1200 requests/min impacted during peak window. affected keys: key-87*, key-3012, key-enterprise-phi. Region eu-west-1 primarily. Not seeing SSO/customer data exposure.

kevin: tagging this as potential regression for quantized handler. I'll bring in eng-ml if we see model kernel exceptions in logs.

mike: logs showing `KVCacheMiss` spikes and `oom` retries on a small subset of pods. throwing `500` with message `runtime: kernel failure`.

sara: applying emergency per-key quota for the top offenders to reduce blast radius:
```
redwoodctl quota set --key key-3012 --rate 10rps --burst 20 --reason "emergency - limit heavy traffic"
redwoodctl quota set --key key-87* --rate 5rps --burst 10 --reason "emergency - limit heavy traffic"
```

ops-bot: quotas applied. Confirmed enforcement at the edge.

marco: are we also removing that variant from any dedicated pools or VPC customers?

sara: leaving dedicated/pinned capacity untouched for now — that could break cherrypicks. For public routing we set weight=0 which should stop new routed traffic.

jess: after weight 0, are we draining in-place or evicting pods? we should avoid OOM evictions.

mike: drain only. control-plane will let in-flight requests finish; draining pods will free KV caches gradually.

sara: stats update: after weight=0 and quotas, 5xx rate down to +3% over baseline, median latency back near normal. still watching tail.

incident-bot: Reminder: run incident checklist and annotate timeline. Create a followup task for postmortem.

sara: doing quick mitigation note for customers: "We temporarily routed traffic off variant `rwd-llama-lite-v2f` due to elevated errors and latency. Traffic has been moved to `stable-llama-v2` and rate limits applied to the heaviest API keys while we investigate. If you see errors, please open a support ticket and include your API key id." Posting to status page after we confirm stability.

jess: I'll pick up the handoff in 20m. Sara, please include logs pointers and the exact rollout command in the handoff message.

sara: copying log links: https://logs.redwood.internal/streams/rlv2f/2168881234 and snippet of recent pod errors:
```
2026-03-15T03:12:11Z pod-42 kernel: runtime error: quant-kernel: invalid shape for fused-attention
2026-03-15T03:12:12Z pod-42 rwd-server: 500 "kernel failure" trace_id=abc123
```

kevin: eng-ml will run a quick kernel validation on v2f and check recent changes to quantized paths. adding @eng-ml oncall.

jess: taking over. Sara — leaving ack, will coordinate customer comms and assign postmortem. To-do for next shift: 1) reproduce kernel failure in staging with same traffic pattern 2) validate quant kernels 3) decide whether to re-introduce v2f with throttles or keep shelved.

sara: handoff complete. leaving the thread to jess. I put a short mitigations summary in the incident doc: https://incidents.internal/2168881234-mitigation.

jess: current status: mitigation successful, v2f weight=0, emergency quotas active for keys [key-3012,key-87*]. We will keep the variant disabled for at least 4 hours while eng-ml validates kernel fixes. If no regressions, plan a controlled canary with traffic shaping and low percent weight.

ops-bot: scheduled checkpoint in 2 hrs. Reminder: if we see reactivation, please create a separate thread for rollback-to-stable.

mike: also flagging billing impact: customers throttled may see increased latency or 429s; product should prepare a goodwill credit plan if major customers impacted.

jess: noted. tagging growth and support for outreach. I'll update status page now.

incident-bot: incident state -> mitigated. Severity -> S2. Next steps -> postmortem and kernel validation.

jess: assigning postmortem owners: kevin (eng-ml), mike (eng-runtime), sara (ops). Timeline doc and next steps will be added to the incident ticket.

marco: thanks team. re-opening if anything changes. :thumbsup:
